title: Observability dashboards for perf-canary (per-model triage views)
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
Build the Grafana dashboards needed to triage perf-canary regressions quickly (runtime + SRE). These dashboards are the primary link targets from perf-canary alerts / incident-bot threads.

Background
Perf-canary emits synthetic traffic against a curated model set and evaluates regressions vs baselines. We need standardized panels to answer: is it real, where is time going (queue vs runtime), and what changed (kernel selection, runtime build, hardware SKU, region).

Scope
- Add/ship a "Perf Canary: Overview" dashboard for rapid scanning across models/regions.
- Add/ship a "Perf Canary: Model Detail" dashboard for a single model+version with deeper attribution.
- Ensure alerts include deep links to the right dashboard + pre-filled variables.
- Keep label/cardinality safe (no per-prompt/per-request dimensions; avoid unbounded tags).

Required variables (templating)
- region (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- tier/pool (hosted | dedicated, and/or pool name if bounded)
- model (canonical model id)
- model_version (registry version string)
- runtime_build_id
- kernel_id / kernel_variant (bounded)
- hardware_sku (A100-80G, H100-SXM, etc.)

Required panels (minimum)
1) End-to-end latency: p50/p95/p99 (time series) + regression band overlay where possible
2) Runtime-only latency: p50/p95/p99
3) Breakdown: prefill latency, decode latency, scheduler queueing time (stacked or aligned)
4) Tokens/sec (throughput) + tokens/sec per GPU (if available)
5) Batch size distribution (p50/p95 + histogram or heatmap)
6) Queue depth / saturation signal (if exported) + request rate for canary traffic
7) KV cache hit-rate (where applicable) and cache-related lat deltas
8) Error rate / non-2xx (should be near 0; includes timeouts)
9) Baseline vs observed summary table (last 30m/2h) with min sample size status
10) Change correlation panels: runtime_build_id and kernel_id as annotations; optional fleet change annotations if we can consume them

Nice-to-have panels
- Telemetry pipeline latency (to explain delayed alerts)
- Control-plane rollout state (what % is on new runtime build in region)

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboards merged into observability-pack with consistent naming, tags, and runbook links.
- Alert payloads (incident-bot) link to Model Detail dashboard with model+region pre-selected.
- Includes a table/panel that makes it obvious when min sample size is not met (avoid false-positive triage churn).
- Reviewed by SRE (paging hygiene) and runtime (attribution usefulness).

Links
- Design doc (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/perf-regression-canary-design.json
- Cardinality audit (Drive): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/perf-canary-metrics-cardinality-audit.json
- Runbook (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert.json
comments: 2026-01-08 (Noah Patel): Creating this as the tracking issue for dashboard work landing in observability-pack. We need a consistent set of panels before we enable paging in us-east phase 1. Primary consumers: #eng-runtime + SRE oncall. Please keep templating constrained to bounded labels (model/model_version/region/hardware_sku/runtime_build_id/kernel_id).

2026-01-10 (Caleb Johnson): Started a draft dashboard JSON with two views: Overview + Model Detail. Open question: do we want model_version as default variable or inferred from model? I’m leaning explicit model_version to avoid confusing overlays when a rollout is mid-flight.

2026-01-13 (Allison Grant): Reminder: any dashboard linked from a page must have (1) a clear 'is this actionable?' header row, (2) direct links to runbook + relevant logs/traces. Also please add a "min samples" panel so oncall can immediately see if alert is underpowered.

2026-01-15 (Logan Wright): Cardinality: do NOT include request_id, prompt_shape_id, or seed as labels. If you need prompt buckets, use a fixed enum like {short, medium, long} and keep it only on a subset of metrics (not histograms).

2026-01-18 (Caleb Johnson): Wired scheduler queueing time panels assuming ENG-4875 lands with metric: runtime_scheduler_queueing_ms histogram. If naming differs, I’ll adapt. Also planning a batch size heatmap but will default to p50/p95 if heatmap query costs are high.

2026-01-23 (Aisha Bello): For paging hygiene, the Model Detail view should include: last 2h summary vs baseline, and a 'what changed' section. If we can’t annotate fleet changes yet, at least show runtime_build_id + kernel_id as a table of top values over time (e.g., topk) so we can spot a flip.

2026-01-27 (Caleb Johnson): PR opened in observability-pack with initial panels + variables and runbook link placeholders: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-19174-perf-canary-dashboard-panels.json. Requesting reviews from Allison + Sofia (triage flow).

2026-01-29 (Sofia Ivanova): Reviewed PR-19174. Requested changes: (1) make queueing-time panel visually prominent near the top; (2) add separate prefill vs decode panels (decode p95 tends to hide in totals); (3) add a batch-size distribution panel broken down by hardware_sku when variable is set.

2026-02-02 (Caleb Johnson): Updated PR with: queueing time moved into header row; separate prefill/decode charts; added a 'top values' table for runtime_build_id/kernel_id/hardware_sku. Kept it bounded (no unbounded label expansions).

2026-02-05 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall workflow note: make sure dashboard URLs are stable and support region variable in the query string. Incident-bot will deep link; if we change variable names later we’ll break pages. Please coordinate variable naming with alert payload format.

2026-02-06 (Caleb Johnson): Coordinated with incident-bot formatting work. Variable names locked to: region, model, model_version, hardware_sku, runtime_build_id, kernel_id. Adding a small 'Links' panel with runbook + logs + traces placeholders. Alert handler PR is separate: sources/github/incident-bot/pr-18603-add-perf-canary-alert-handler.json
2026-02-10 (Allison Grant): Approved after adding 'Min sample size met?' singlestat and a panel to display canary QPS/capacity budget (helps confirm canary isn’t accidentally fanning out).

2026-02-14 (Caleb Johnson): PR merged. Dashboards now available in prod Grafana under folder: Runtime / Perf Canary. Next: ensure alert rules include these links (tracked in ENG-4878). Closing this ticket.
